applicability.action: report an error finding when a selected existing package.json is not valid JSON
applicability.exceptions: missing files return no finding
applicability.loading: script

distinguishing_scenario: package.json with a trailing comma and only exact versions: no registered rule is violated, the checker reports 'package.json is not valid JSON'.
proposed_clause_text: A package.json that is not valid JSON is reported as an error finding instead of being skipped.
rationale: check-manifests.cjs:130-136 verified. Both Claude runs noted 'invalid JSON is an error' only in IMPLEMENTATION coverage notes; the K1 groups cover when checks run (FG-K1-6bce8e2857), version rules (FG-K1-4a6d4edee1), NUL decoding and walks (FG-K1-3e3bd27c1f) and per-file argument handling (FG-K1-7d8a86c09f). An unparsable package.json fails the check even without any dependency violation, so this is an unrepresented designed acceptance gate (consistent with candidate K0's manifest-readability proposals).
status_note: Proposal only: not a confirmed EXTRA, not an oracle mapping, not a cross-candidate comparison.
trigger_scope: check-manifests run on an existing package.json

applicability.action: report an error finding when reading/parsing an existing selected manifest throws
applicability.exceptions: missing files return no finding
applicability.loading: script
applicability.trigger: checking an existing .csproj, Directory.Packages.props or package.json

distinguishing_scenario: An existing .csproj that the checker cannot read: instead of 'no findings' the checker reports 'manifest could not be read'.
proposed_clause_text: A recognised manifest that the checker cannot read or parse is reported as an error finding ('manifest could not be read'), not as a clean result.
rationale: check-manifests.cjs:163-172 verified: any exception from the per-type checker (read failure, undecodable text, malformed XML tag thrown by the reader) becomes an error finding. The Codex groups FG-K1-3e3bd27c1f (decoding rejects NUL input) and FG-K1-6e757edf58 (minimal XML reader) describe causes of such exceptions but not the resulting checker error; no group states that an unreadable manifest fails the check. Distinct gate, consistent with candidate K0.
status_note: Proposal only: not a confirmed EXTRA, not an oracle mapping, not a cross-candidate comparison.
trigger_scope: check-manifests run on an existing recognised manifest

applicability.trigger: frontend workspace exists and package integrity or unexpected dependency changes are relevant

distinguishing_scenario: An unexpectedly changed lockfile is not inspected during the frontend dependency scan although npm audit runs.

evidence.exact_excerpt: When a frontend workspace exists, run `npm audit`. Distinguish production from development/build dependencies and direct from transitive packages: a development-only vulnerability can still matter to the supply chain, but its runtime impact differs from a browser-shipped dependency. Review lockfiles when package integrity or unexpected dependency changes are relevant.
